newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market declined sharply on Thursday, with both the long term future and the peseta slipping to key levels not seen since January 10.
The 10-yr future was trading at 113.88, down 41 points from Wednesday's close, while the peseta was trading at 84.05/09 versus the mark, above the key 84.00 level.
"Foreign investors decided Bonos were overdone, so they took profits and moved part of their funds into other European markets," a dealer in Madrid said.
"But this is only a consolidation, not a serious change in overall market's mood," said Luca Jellinek analyst at Paribas.
The 10-year spread over Bunds widened to 94 basis points from 90 basis points on Wednesday, while the differential over US Treasuries turned positive at around two basis points.
Falling under a weakened peseta, the yield curve flattened a little. The two- to 10-year yield spread decreased to 139 basis points from 143 bps yesterday.
